sections.h2: What are the ways to sell a house in Macon, Georgia?
sections.html:
A Macon seller can list with an agent, sell without one, or accept a cash offer from a buyer who purchases the house as it stands. The right route depends mostly on the condition of the house and how soon the money is needed.

  • Listing with an agent: usually the best price when the house shows well, with the longest timeline and the most preparation.
  • Selling on your own: saves the agent's fee, though you handle showings, contracts and buyer questions yourself.
  • Cash sale as-is: suits vacant, inherited, tax-delinquent or storm-worn houses, where repairs would cost more than the discount you give up.

A buyer paying cash can skip the appraisal and loan approval steps that often hold up a financed purchase. That matters most when the house has deferred repairs, because a lender's appraiser may flag the same items an inspector does.

sections.h2: How large is Macon and what do the housing numbers say?
sections.html:
Macon is governed as Macon-Bibb County, a single consolidated government, so the Census Bureau reports its figures at the county level. The July 1, 2025 estimate is 157,556 residents, almost level with the 157,346 counted on April 1, 2020.

The Census table also shows how much the map changed. Land area is listed at 55.72 square miles for 2010 and 249.38 square miles for 2020, and the count of residents went from 91,351 to 157,346 over those same two census years. A 2014 county notice about assessments refers to the "consolidation of the governments," which matches that jump.

  • Median value of an owner-occupied home, 2020 to 2024: $174,500.
  • Share of homes lived in by their owners: 51.4%.
  • Median gross rent: $1,066 a month.
  • Median household income: $51,234, with 24.7% of residents in poverty.
  • Mean commute: 22.2 minutes.

With a median value of $174,500, repair costs take a larger bite out of a Macon sale than in higher-priced Georgia cities. Compare any offer to recent sales on your own street, since values can differ a lot from one neighborhood to the next.

sections.h2: What older neighborhoods and landmarks shape Macon real estate?
sections.html:
Macon's historic core affects what owners may do to a building. County Planning and Zoning has been updating design guidelines for the central business districts and the historic districts, naming Intown, the Central Business District, Vineville and Cherokee Heights. Those guidelines cover changes to building exteriors, new construction and demolitions.

If your house sits inside one of those districts, ask Macon-Bibb Planning and Zoning what review applies before you promise a buyer anything about exterior work, and before you agree to a repair credit that involves siding, windows or porches.

Macon also holds a major archaeological site. Ocmulgee Mounds National Historical Park, at 1207 Emery Highway, is described by the National Park Service as the site of the largest archaeology dig in American history, with more than 800 men working and about 3 million artifacts found.

sections.h2: What happens to a vacant or run-down house in Macon-Bibb County?
sections.html:
The county treats abandoned and unsafe buildings seriously, and a vacant house can pick up tax consequences or a demolition order if it is left alone. Macon-Bibb's "Blight Fight" page says a property counts as blight when it meets at least two listed criteria, such as being uninhabitable or abandoned, having severely overgrown vegetation at 12 inches or higher, or failing to meet code for at least one year after written notice.

An unkempt yard alone is not treated as blight, and loose animals and abandoned vehicles are handled by other offices. For a property reported as blighted, the Office of the Mayor may send a "nuisance per se" letter, and the owner may then repair or demolish the structure. If the owner does neither, the county may proceed with demolition.

Under the county's blight tax process the property must be vacant, the owner may appeal the designation, and properties not appealed can be placed on a list sent to the Tax Commissioner each August. Code Enforcement takes reports and completion notices at 478-803-0470. If you inherited a house that has sat empty, resolving a notice before you sell avoids a surprise at closing, and a cash buyer will usually price a pending notice into the offer rather than refuse it.

sections.h2: How do Bibb County assessments, appeals and exemptions work for sellers?
sections.html:
The Macon-Bibb County Board of Tax Assessors mails a state-required notice of assessment each year to the owner of record. The 2025 notices went out on May 16, 2025, based on a January 1, 2025 valuation date, and the notice carries a 45-day window for a written appeal.

The Board's own summary says an appeal letter must name the route the owner chooses, and that appeals must be hand delivered or mailed with a dated postmark because emails and faxes are not accepted. The three routes work differently:

Appeal routes after a Bibb County notice of assessment (Macon-Bibb Board of Tax Assessors summary)
RouteWhat it coversCost note
Board of EqualizationAny property; grounds limited to value or uniformityNo cost unless an agent is hired
Hearing officerNon-homesteaded real property and large wireless personal propertyNo cost unless an agent is hired
Nonbinding arbitrationReal property valuation only; owner supplies a certified appraisalThe party farthest from the final value pays the arbitrator

Either side may take a Board of Equalization decision to superior court within 30 days. For homeowners, the county's September 2025 resolution says the residential homestead exemption stands at $7,000 and that officials asked the local legislative delegation for added exemptions at ages 65, 75 and 85. Because a new local exemption needs a local act and a ballot vote, ask the Board of Assessors whether the senior tiers are in effect before you count on them.

The Board is at 688 Walnut Street, Suite 200, phone 478-200-5550. The Tax Commissioner is at 610 Mulberry Street, phone 478-621-6500. Ask the Tax Commissioner for the current bill and any balance before you set a closing date.

sections.h2: What does the Georgia transfer tax mean for a Macon sale?
sections.html:
Georgia charges a real estate transfer tax when title changes hands, and the deed cannot be recorded with the Clerk of Superior Court until it is paid. The Department of Revenue prints the rate as $1 for the first $1,000 or fractional part of $1,000, and 10 cents for each additional $100 or fractional part of $100.

The seller is liable under the statute, O.C.G.A. 48-6-1 through 48-6-10, though the Department notes that sales contracts often shift payment to the buyer. The form is the PT-61, completed online through the Georgia Superior Court Clerks' Cooperative Authority. For questions on exemptions, the Department points to the Clerk of Superior Court in the county where the property sits, which for Macon is Bibb County.

faqs.q: Can I sell my house in Macon if it is vacant or has code violations?
faqs.a: Yes. A vacant house can be sold, but clear or disclose any county notice first. If Code Enforcement has flagged the property as blight, follow the instructions in the letter and report completion at 478-803-0470, or tell the buyer about the open notice. A cash buyer will often take the house with the notice still open and adjust the price.

faqs.q: How long do I have to appeal my Macon-Bibb assessment?
faqs.a: You have 45 days from the date of the notice, and the appeal must be in writing. The Board of Tax Assessors says to hand deliver the letter or mail it with a dated postmark, and it does not accept email or fax. Name your chosen route in the letter.

faqs.q: Does Macon-Bibb County offer a homestead exemption?
faqs.a: Yes. A county announcement from September 2025 says residents can claim a $7,000 exemption on a residential homestead. The county also asked state legislators for extra exemptions at ages 65, 75 and 85, which need a local act and a ballot vote, so ask the Board of Assessors what applies to you.

faqs.q: Who pays the Georgia transfer tax when a Macon house sells?
faqs.a: The seller is liable by statute, although many contracts assign the cost to the buyer. The rate is printed on the Department of Revenue page as $1 for the first $1,000 and 10 cents per additional $100, counting fractions as whole units. Check the contract and ask the Bibb County Clerk of Superior Court about exemptions.

faqs.q: What documents should I gather before selling a Macon house?
faqs.a: Collect the deed, your latest assessment notice and tax bill, any code or blight letters, and mortgage payoff details. Add a list of repairs you know about. Having these ready speeds up a cash offer and keeps a listed sale from stalling at closing.
